question.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $(2u)\cdot u,$ we multiply $u\cdot u$ by $2.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2u)\cdot u & =2(u\cdot u) \\  & =2\cdot 27 \\  & =54.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $u\cdot (3v),$ we compute $u\cdot v$ first and then multiply the result by $3.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (3v) & =3(u\cdot v) \\  & =3({u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4}) \\  & =3(2\cdot (-3)+3\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 2) \\  & =3(-6-6-1-6-6) \\  & =3\cdot (-25) \\  & =-75.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{(2u)\cdot u}{u\cdot (3v)}=\frac{54}{-75}=-\frac{18}{25}.
$$
